diagnosis: HBV calibrated on 1971-1997 daily data (one warm-up year) using about 8,500 DDS runs that maximised NSE. The result is NSE ≈ 0.79, KGE ≈ 0.78, r ≈ 0.89 and PBIAS ≈ +5%, so the model slightly overestimates total flow. The catchment is a small, flashy lowland area on clay with some urban land. The best fit has a fast response (MAXBAS ≈ 1.7, K1 ≈ 0.22, K0 ≈ 0.31 with a low UZL ≈ 6), a highly non-linear soil (BETA ≈ 6.4, FC ≈ 260 mm, LP ≈ 1.0) and a very slow groundwater store (K2 ≈ 0.0013/day). That store supplies a small but persistent baseflow and takes years to settle. I set its initial level (160 mm) close to its long-term mean so the run starts near equilibrium. Snow hardly matters here (about 2% of precipitation falls as snow), so the snow parameters are poorly identified and CFMAX/CFR sit at their range limits with little effect. Expected weaknesses: peak sizes in summer storms, especially on urban and cracking-clay soils; recessions after dry summers; and when autumn wetting-up starts. The parameter sets from the later calibration rounds were very similar, which suggests a stable optimum. However, BETA, FC and K2 trade off against each other, and the slow store makes results depend on how the scored period is initialised. I did not run a split-sample test. I'm moderately confident and expect independent-period NSE of roughly 0.7–0.8.
